title: Myelopathy / transverse myelitis workup
consultQuestion: Spinal cord syndrome — compressive, vascular, nutritional, or inflammatory?
keyHistory: Tempo: hyperacute (minutes — infarct), hours–days (myelitis), weeks–months (DAVF, nutritional, spondylotic)
Bariatric surgery, malabsorption, zinc products, nitrous oxide
Optic neuritis, area postrema symptoms (NMOSD), prior demyelinating events (MS)
Systemic disease: sarcoid, lupus, Sjögren, cancer
keyExam: Pattern: anterior (spared vibration/proprioception — anterior spinal artery), posterior columns (B12, copper)
UMN signs; may be areflexic acutely
redFlags: Compressive lesion on MRI — neurosurgery now
Hyperacute onset with back pain — cord infarct or hematoma
Area postrema or optic neuritis — NMOSD

clues: Hyperacute, aortic procedure; anterior pencil-like T2, DWI restriction
Man >50, subacute progression; central T2 often to the conus, flow voids; spinal angiogram
Longitudinally extensive (≥3 segments) lesion; AQP4/MOG antibodies
Short (<2 segments), peripheral lesions; brain lesions; oligoclonal bands

differential.dx: B12 deficiency / nitrous oxide / copper deficiency
clues: Posterior ± lateral columns, inverted-V; MMA/homocysteine; copper/ceruloplasmin
Nitrous oxide: serum B12 low in only 42% of users; homocysteine and MMA raised in ~80% (Ménétrier 2023)
Copper: prior gastric/bariatric surgery, malabsorption, excess zinc (supplements, denture cream); cytopenias often but not always (Kumar 2006)

differential.dx: Neurosarcoidosis, infection (HIV, HTLV-1, syphilis, VZV), paraneoplastic, spondylotic myelopathy with enhancement

workup.test: MRI entire spine with and without gadolinium
notes: Image the whole cord — a thoracic sensory level can come from a cervical lesion (Frohman 2010); DWI for suspected infarct (Douglas 2022)

workup.test: LP: cells, protein, glucose, oligoclonal bands, IgG index, cytology, infectious studies
notes: Pleocytosis or raised IgG index supports myelitis (Frohman 2010)

workup.test: B12, MMA, homocysteine; copper, ceruloplasmin, zinc
notes: Nitrous oxide: don't rely on total B12 — send MMA and homocysteine; interpret with eGFR, both rise in kidney disease (Ménétrier 2023)
Copper deficiency: zinc may be high even without supplements; B12 deficiency can coexist (Kumar 2006)

workup.test: ACE / chest CT for sarcoidosis; ANA/SSA/SSB
notes: Autoantibodies alone don't prove a connective-tissue cause — they occur in MS and NMOSD (Frohman 2010)
ACE is insufficiently sensitive and specific in serum and CSF; ACE, CRP, and sIL-2R have no proven value for diagnosing neurosarcoidosis — don't use them to rule it in or out (Stern 2018)
Biopsy an accessible nonneural site to support probable neurosarcoidosis (Stern 2018)

indication: Cancer risk or LETM without AQP4/MOG

decisionRules.recommendation: Exclude compression first with whole-spine MRI

decisionRules.condition: Transverse myelitis criteria: bilateral sensory/motor/autonomic cord dysfunction with sensory level, peak 4 h–21 days, plus inflammation (CSF pleocytosis or raised IgG index, or gadolinium-enhancing lesion), with compressive, radiation, neoplastic and vascular causes excluded
evidenceNote: Transverse Myelitis Consortium criteria, Frohman 2010 Table 1

decisionRules.recommendation: Test AQP4-IgG and MOG-IgG; NMOSD likely if AQP4-positive
Reconsider myelopathy — central or peripheral alternative

initialSteps: Copper deficiency (Kumar/Mayo practice): elemental copper 6 mg/day PO for 1 week, 4 mg/day for 1 week, then 2 mg/day; stop excess zinc (stopping zinc alone may suffice); recheck serum copper
recsTemplate: MRI entire spine with and without contrast; MRI brain with contrast
LP: cells, protein, glucose, OCB, IgG index, cytology, infectious studies
B12, MMA, homocysteine, copper, ceruloplasmin, zinc, HIV, HTLV-1, RPR
pearls: Spondylotic myelopathy can show pancake-like transverse enhancement and mimic myelitis (Douglas 2022)
Cord infarct imaging can be normal early — DWI is more sensitive (Douglas 2022)
Cavernous malformations: stepwise episodes with recovery; popcorn lesions with GRE blooming (Douglas 2022)
Copper deficiency myelopathy mimics subacute combined degeneration — dorsal-column T2 signal, usually cervical, no enhancement (Kumar 2006)
Copper replacement: blood counts recover promptly; neurological recovery is variable but progression usually halts (Kumar 2006)
Ongoing decline after B12 replacement with a normal B12 level → check copper (Kumar 2006)
sources: Frohman EM, Wingerchuk DM. Transverse Myelitis. N Engl J Med 2010;363:564-572
Douglas AG, Xu DJ, Shah MP. Approach to Myelopathy and Myelitis. Neurol Clin 2022;40:133-156. doi:10.1016/j.ncl.2021.08.009
Kumar N. Copper Deficiency Myelopathy (Human Swayback). Mayo Clin Proc 2006;81:1371-1384

Ménétrier T, Denimal D. Vitamin B12 Status in Recreational Users of Nitrous Oxide: A Systematic Review Focusing on the Prevalence of Laboratory Abnormalities. Antioxidants 2023;12:1191. doi:10.3390/antiox12061191
Stern BJ, et al. Definition and Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Neurosarcoidosis. JAMA Neurol 2018;75:1546-1553. doi:10.1001/jamaneurol.2018.2295
